html:
SMTO-BOOT-0012 — The AI model's files weren't found on this computer

GUID: a2d5660e-fb9b-4209-becb-0a9138defe9a
Slug: boot-model-file-missing
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The model start script couldn't find or read the model file it was set to load, or for vLLM the matching tokenizer files. It stopped before loading anything, and files already on disk weren't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Read the terminal message: it shows the model file path the script tried, or says the model wasn't found in the download folder. Scripts search a default download folder unless you point them at a specific file.
  2. If the model hasn't been downloaded yet, download the exact model file the script expects before running it. Most of these start scripts never download the model for you.
  3. If the file is somewhere else, set MODEL_FILE (or MODEL_PATH for some scripts) to its full location, and make sure your account can read it. The script loads only the file it's told about and stops if it can't read it.
  4. For vLLM scripts that mention the tokenizer, also set TOKENIZER_PATH to the downloaded folder that holds the model's tokenizer and config files. vLLM needs those files separately, so fixing the model path alone won't fix this.

What success looks like

  • The script shows the model file it's using and the engine starts loading the model.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal output, including the Error reference line, and send it to the person who maintains the model setup after removing tokens and private folder names. Don't delete the model download folder; its files may just be incomplete.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A model launcher could not find or read the selected weights file (MODEL_FILE, MODEL_PATH or its Hugging Face cache search under HF_HOME) or, for vLLM GGUF profiles, the base tokenizer/config snapshot, and exited before serving the model.

What this means

  • Model launch cannot find/read the selected weights file or cannot locate the required local tokenizer snapshot. The selected launcher stops before serving the requested model. Existing weights, tokenizer files and caches remain on disk. A missing path or tokenizer file does not establish whether an existing download is complete or whether the selected model is supported.

Why this can happen

  • Model launch cannot find/read the selected weights file or cannot locate the required local tokenizer snapshot.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish model weights from tokenizer files and inspect the exact selected path/cache.

How to fix it

  • Check the path in the technical detail (ls -l, read permission) or the cache under $HF_HOME/hub and ~/.cache/huggingface/hub; export MODEL_FILE (MODEL_PATH for the Qwen3.8 Flash profile) to complete, readable weights and TOKENIZER_PATH to a snapshot containing tokenizer.json and config.json, then relaunch. Existing caches are left untouched, so verify download completeness separately.
  • Select complete readable weights with MODEL_FILE/MODEL_PATH and the required tokenizer snapshot with TOKENIZER_PATH when reported.

Retry and execution caution

  • Select the intended existing model file and required tokenizer snapshot; verify the paths before starting the model again.

How to verify the fix

  • Complete readable weights and any required tokenizer snapshot are selected.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The selected launcher stops before serving the requested model. Existing weights, tokenizer files and caches remain on disk.
  • A missing path or tokenizer file does not establish whether an existing download is complete or whether the selected model is supported.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
